subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 30-year-old man receives a high-protein diet during a metabolic study. In his hepatocytes, citrulline is converted to argininosuccinate in a reaction that incorporates aspartate and cleaves a molecule of ATP to AMP and pyrophosphate.
question: Which enzyme catalyzes this reaction?
explanation_correct: Argininosuccinate synthetase ligates citrulline and aspartate to form argininosuccinate in the cytosol, using ATP that is hydrolyzed to AMP and pyrophosphate. This is the second ATP-consuming step of the urea cycle and the point at which the second nitrogen enters.

explanation_incorrect.A: Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I condenses ammonia with bicarbonate in the mitochondrial matrix and hydrolyzes two ATP to ADP, but it does not use citrulline or aspartate.
explanation_incorrect.B: Ornithine transcarbamylase transfers carbamoyl phosphate to ornithine and consumes no ATP.
explanation_incorrect.D: Argininosuccinate lyase cleaves argininosuccinate to arginine and fumarate in an ATP-independent reaction.
explanation_incorrect.E: Arginase hydrolyzes arginine to urea and ornithine without using ATP.

educationalObjective: Argininosuccinate synthetase incorporates aspartate into the urea cycle and is the step in which ATP is cleaved to AMP and pyrophosphate.
